articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a biblical 167 security fixes including a SharePoint zero-day called 'BlueHammer' - because apparently even Patch Tuesday needs steroids now. Chrome's fourth zero-day of the month is just the cherry on this vulnerability sundae.

articles.title: The Internet Still Works: SmugMug Powers Online Photography
articles.summary: Congress rushes to rubber-stamp another surveillance reauthorization disguised as 'accountability' - because nothing says reform like keeping the warrantless spying machine humming. Speaker Johnson's fig leaf is so transparent it's practically glass.

articles.title: Feuding Ransomware Groups Leak Each Other's Data
articles.summary: NSA chief during the Snowden era finally admits they fucked up royally 13 years later. Chris Inglis gets refreshingly honest about how the agency completely mishandled having their digital pants pulled down by one brilliant contractor.

articles.title: CIA Ran MK-ULTRA Experiments on Prisoners of War in U.S. Custody, Declassified Docs Confirm
articles.summary: Four Democrats hold the keys to Trump's domestic surveillance kingdom, and privacy advocates are sweating bullets. It's democracy by committee, where the committee decides if the government gets to read your texts without asking.

articles.title: 30 ClawHub skills secretly turn AI agents into a crypto swarm
articles.summary: Declassified docs confirm the CIA ran MK-ULTRA mind control experiments on POWs because apparently regular war crimes weren't creative enough. The agency that brought you psychological torture now has the receipts in black and white.

articles.title: Researchers Discover Critical GitHub CVE-2026-3854 RCE Flaw Exploitable via Single Git Push
articles.summary: LiteLLM gets pwned via SQL injection within 36 hours of disclosure - proving hackers have better patch management than most enterprises. Nothing says 'critical infrastructure' like a database that falls over faster than a house of cards.

articles.title: Brazilian LofyGang Resurfaces After Three Years With Minecraft LofyStealer Campaign
articles.summary: GitHub's latest gift to humanity: remote code execution with a single git push command. Because apparently version control wasn't dangerous enough without letting randos execute arbitrary code on your servers.

articles.title: Why Secure Data Movement Is the Zero Trust Bottleneck Nobody Talks About
articles.summary: VECT 2.0 ransomware is so broken it permanently destroys files over 131KB - it's not ransomware, it's digital arson with a payment portal. Even paying the ransom won't save you from these criminal masterminds who can't code.

articles.title: ShinyHunters Leaks Data of Udemy, Zara, 7-Eleven in Salesforce Linked Breach
articles.summary: Medical device giant Medtronic admits breach after ShinyHunters claims 9+ million records stolen. Nothing says 'patient safety' like having your pacemaker data traded on underground forums.

articles.title: Daily Hacker News for 2026-04-24
articles.summary: TeamPCP supply chain campaign returns from 26-day vacation with a vengeance, hitting Checkmarx, Bitwarden, and spawning npm worms. When hackers take breaks longer than your DevOps team, you know the ecosystem is fucked.
